client_profile:
Across Acme Eye Care Foundation, Acme Trust and Acme Clinics LLP, personal data arises throughout the eye-care continuum: registration and consent forms at vision screening and outreach camps, electronic health records and surgical details, imaging and biometric identifiers used in teleophthalmology, and donor, employee and volunteer records. As Data Fiduciaries under the DPDP Act, each entity must map these flows, issue clear notices, establish valid consent for health data, and honour withdrawal, access, correction and erasure rights.

The assessment would evaluate purpose limitation, retention standards, security safeguards, breach reporting to the Data Protection Board, and data-sharing arrangements with hospitals, insurers and technology partners. Given large-scale processing of vulnerable rural beneficiaries and children's data, the foundation should also weigh Significant Data Fiduciary duties such as DPIAs and audits, ensuring the Trust's programs and the LLP's clinical operations maintain consistent, auditable compliance.

categories.title: Patient Identity Data
categories.summary: Basic identifiers of patients visiting Acme Clinics LLP facilities for consultations, surgeries and diagnostics.
bullets: Full name, age/date of birth, gender and photograph at registration
Government ID references (Aadhaar, voter ID, ration card) for patient verification
Permanent and current address, including rural/tribal location for outreach cases
Emergency contact and next-of-kin details

categories.title: Health & Ophthalmic Records
categories.summary: Detailed medical data generated through eye examinations, diagnoses, surgeries and post-operative follow-up care.
bullets: Diagnoses such as cataract, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, refractive errors and corneal conditions
Visual acuity readings, intraocular pressure, prescriptions and spectacle power records
Surgical records, consent forms, implant/lens details and operative notes
Medical history, comorbidities (e.g. diabetes) and current medications
Follow-up visit notes, complications and referral records to partner hospitals

categories.title: Ocular Imaging & Biometrics
categories.summary: Specialised eye imaging and biometric measurements captured during diagnosis and pre-surgical workups.
bullets: Retinal fundus photographs and OCT scans
Corneal topography, pachymetry and IOL biometry measurements
Anterior segment images and slit-lamp photographs
Potential linkage with ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) identifiers

categories.title: Community Outreach Beneficiaries
categories.summary: Data on free-surgery beneficiaries and camp attendees collected through the Trust's community screening programmes.
bullets: Camp registration forms with name, village, income category and BPL/ration card details
School and workplace screening records, including children's data requiring parental consent
Transport, food and accommodation arrangements for rural camp patients
Post-camp outcome tracking, vision-restored reporting and impact documentation
Consent and declaration forms for free surgeries and photograph usage in reports

categories.title: Donor & Financial Data
categories.summary: Personal and payment information of donors supporting the Trust's charitable eye-care initiatives.
bullets: Donor name, PAN, contact details and donation receipts for 80G claims
Bank account, UPI, card and cheque details for contribution processing
Corporate CSR partnership contacts and funding documentation
Grant-making foundation due-diligence records

categories.title: Billing & Insurance Data
categories.summary: Financial and scheme-related records tied to patient treatment at the LLP's clinics.
bullets: Insurance and TPA claim details for eligible procedures
Government scheme beneficiaries (e.g. state cataract surgery schemes, PMJAY)
Payment receipts, invoices and outstanding dues
Tax invoices with GST and patient billing address

categories.title: Staff, Doctors & Volunteers
categories.summary: Employment and engagement records of the Trust's and LLP's workforce, including visiting specialists and camp volunteers.
bullets: Employee records: name, address, salary, bank details, Aadhaar/PF references
Doctor credentials, medical council registration and qualification certificates
Volunteer and field-worker details for outreach camps
Attendance, duty rosters and performance records

categories.title: Digital & Communication Data
categories.summary: Personal data captured through the acme.example website, appointment channels and patient communication.
bullets: Website contact and appointment request forms (name, phone, email, query text)
Cookies, IP address, device and usage analytics on the website
Call recordings and WhatsApp/SMS correspondence for appointments and reminders
Grievance and feedback submissions, including nodal grievance officer correspondence

processing_bullets: Personal data is collected from patients, beneficiaries, donors, employees and volunteers through clinic registrations, outreach camps, eye-screening programs, websites and physical application forms.
Health-related data, including ocular records, diagnostic results and treatment history, is processed by Acme Clinics LLP for diagnosis, treatment, referral and continuity of patient care.
Data collected by Acme Trust during community outreach and screening camps is shared with Acme Clinics LLP and partner institutions for referrals and follow-up services.
Collection relies on consent and notice mechanisms across digital and offline channels, as required under DPDP obligations for processing personal data of beneficiaries and patients.
Personal data is retained in electronic health records, physical case files and donor databases, with retention periods governed by clinical, statutory, contractual and programmatic requirements.

Third-party service providers, including IT vendors, cloud hosting partners, laboratories and outreach partners, process personal data under contractual data protection and confidentiality obligations.
Personal data may be accessed across multiple clinic locations, field offices and program sites, necessitating role-based access controls, audit trails and secure authentication.
Donor and funding-related data is shared with government authorities, statutory bodies and funding partners for grants, reporting, audit and regulatory compliance purposes.

Sensitive personal data, particularly health data of vulnerable beneficiaries including minors and the elderly, is safeguarded through encryption, access restriction, retention limits and breach-response measures.
